importance_ranking.reason: Portable pantry cabins vary significantly in visual type — basic site canteen shell vs fitted office pantry with counter and overhead cabinets vs container-based unit. Buyers use the listing image to identify whether the product matches their deployment context before reading any text. Wrong visual type is an immediate skip.

Pantry size (floor area) and wall panel material are non-negotiable shortlisting gates — a cabin that does not fit the site footprint or meet the insulation requirement cannot be considered regardless of price. Buyers filter by these specs before contacting any seller.

Price varies substantially with size and panel material — a 20x10 ft PUF-insulated cabin costs multiples of an 8x6 ft GI sheet cabin. Indian B2B buyers compare prices across listings after confirming size and material fit; price is a primary decision lever before contacting sellers.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Standard catalogue sizes are quoted per piece; custom-dimensioned builds are quoted per sq ft by multiple manufacturers. Both units appear in the market — a buyer comparing a per-piece listing with a per-sq-ft listing without unit clarity will misread the price. Unit must be shown alongside price.
importance_ranking.reason: Per piece vs per sq ft ambiguity is a real market condition for this MCAT. Price cannot be compared across listings without knowing the unit, creating a genuine buyer confusion risk.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant brand with buyer recall exists in the Indian portable pantry cabin market — the market is fragmented across regional fabricators and buyers search by size, material, and price rather than manufacturer name.
importance_ranking.reason: Institutional and government buyers evaluate manufacturer status, installation capability, and site delivery track record during vendor selection. For smaller corporate buyers, company is less critical but seller credibility (years in business, past project references) is still checked before placing an order.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Floor area is the primary price driver and is non-interchangeable — a buyer with a specific site footprint requirement cannot substitute one size for another, and price scales directly with cabin area.

Panel material (PUF vs EPS vs GI Sheet vs FRP) determines insulation grade and weather resistance, with PUF-insulated panels commanding a significant price premium over basic GI sheet construction — non-interchangeable across climate and application requirements.

missing_important_specs.why_important: PUF and EPS panels are available in multiple thickness grades (25mm, 40mm, 60mm, 80mm) that determine thermal performance and price independently of panel material type — a critical differentiator for cold-climate mining and food-grade deployments.

Whether the cabin includes basic electrical wiring, full electrical fittings (lighting, switchboard, points), or no electrical work is a buyer decision gate that affects both price and site readiness — currently not captured by any spec in the seller list.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Structural and insulation material determines which product line the seller can offer and is the primary basis for accurate pricing — sellers cannot quote without knowing whether the buyer needs PUF-insulated, FRP, MS, or GI construction.

The scope of internal fittings (unfurnished shell vs work counter vs full fitted pantry) defines a fundamentally different product and price point — sellers need this to scope the build and respond with an accurate quote.

missing_important_specs.why_important: The required floor area is the single most important buyer input — sellers cannot determine product fit or price without knowing the cabin dimensions, and size gates the entire product selection before material or fittings are considered.
